comment: Every upstream this repository vendors, and the exact commit each tree was
taken from. scripts/common/vendor-sync.mjs reads this to fetch a pristine
copy and to materialise a tree; scripts/common/vendor-diff.mjs reads it to
regenerate the patch series; scripts/common/check-vendor.sh reads it to
assert that it still describes the tree, and with --upstream to report
whether upstream has moved past the recorded ref.
base is the commit this tree was last reconciled against. It is NOT what
the tree contains: the tree is ours and carries patches. That is the whole
point of recording it. See patches/README.md.
docs/methodology/vendoring.md is the rule and TODO/vendor.md is the work.

upstreams.name: rustls
upstreams.ref_reason: Upstream's own tag for the newest release. 0.24.0-dev.1 is published on the registry and is a development version rather than a release, so a tree pinned to it would be reconciled against a moving branch.
upstreams.why_vendored: HARNESS-13 terminates a browser's TLS handshake so the HTTP/2 half of a fingerprint can be read. The seam this needs is a server that completes a handshake whose ClientHello has already been read off the socket by this tree's own parser, and patching it here is the ruling recorded in TODO/RULES.md.

exclude_reason..git: The clone's own history. The vendored tree is source in this repository's history, not a nested repository.
exclude_reason..github: Upstream's own CI, which runs against upstream's repository and cannot run here.
exclude_reason.AGENTS.md: An agent instruction file of any name is never vendored: a file with such a name anywhere under a repository is read as instructions by the tools working in it. Excluded by name whether or not upstream has one today, so a release that adds one does not land silently.
exclude_reason.audit: Third-party audit reports about upstream's own releases. Data about upstream's process, not source.
exclude_reason.bogo: The BoringSSL test-suite shim, which needs BoGo itself.
exclude_reason.ci-bench: A benchmark harness that needs valgrind.
exclude_reason.connect-tests: Tests that reach the public internet.
exclude_reason.examples: Upstream's example binaries, which pull clap, env_logger and mio.
exclude_reason.fuzz: cargo-fuzz targets, which need a nightly toolchain. Upstream's own workspace already excludes them from members.
exclude_reason.openssl-tests: Interop tests that need OpenSSL on the machine.
exclude_reason.provider-example: An example of writing a crypto provider.
exclude_reason.rustls-fuzzing-provider: A crypto provider that exists to be fuzzed.
exclude_reason.rustls-post-quantum: A shim crate that is empty since 0.23.22; the feature it wrapped is in rustls itself.
exclude_reason.rustls-provider-test: 5.7 MiB of integration tests for third-party crypto providers. This tree uses the ring provider rustls ships with.
exclude_reason.test-ca: 542 KiB of generated test certificates for workspace members this tree does not vendor. HARNESS-13 mints its own authority per run.
exclude_reason.website: 3.0 MiB of a documentation site. Nothing builds it and nothing here reads it.

not_patched.rustls-test: Kept because rustls's own dev-dependencies name it through the workspace dependency table, and dropping it would mean patching a manifest to run no tests. Not depended on by anything this tree builds.

upstreams.name: h2
upstreams.ref_reason: Upstream's newest release tag. ⚠ The reference sweep read this tree at commit cb9574bb2c18, abbreviated because this project's secret scan refuses a 40-character hex run in prose and references/hyperium__h2/PROVENANCE.md carries it in full. That is a trunk commit rather than a release, so the seam is RE-READ at this tag rather than carried from the sweep's line numbers. TODO/RULES.md rule 3: a document is checked against the tree it describes.
upstreams.why_vendored: EMIT-03. A client that omits the HTTP/2 PRIORITY block carries a zero in one field of four in a widely-read fingerprint, and every profile in this corpus carries the block: six of six, two browsers, two majors, two platforms, one value. ⛔ Upstream will not take the patch for a stated reason rather than by neglect: RFC 9113 deprecates stream priority, so a release adding a way to send one would add a way to do what the specification tells clients not to do. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-04, against the recommendation attached to the question.

exclude_reasons..git: The clone's own history. The vendored tree is source in this repository's history, not a nested repository.
exclude_reasons..github: Upstream's own CI, which runs against upstream's repository and cannot run here.
exclude_reasons.AGENTS.md: An agent instruction file of any name is never vendored: a file with such a name anywhere under a repository is read as instructions by the tools working in it. Excluded by name whether or not upstream has one today, so a release that adds one does not land silently.
exclude_reasons.benches: Upstream's criterion benchmarks, which nothing here runs.
exclude_reasons.examples: Upstream's example binaries, which pull a runtime and a logger this tree does not need.
exclude_reasons.fixtures: The HPACK test-case corpus, one directory per implementation of the same cases. ⭐ It is http2jp/hpack-test-case, which this project already mines separately at references/http2jp__hpack-test-case, so vendoring a second copy would be the same corpus in two places.
exclude_reasons.fuzz: cargo-fuzz targets, which need a nightly toolchain.
exclude_reasons.tests: Upstream's integration suite, which needs h2-support and a full tokio test rig. ⚠ What this project asserts about the patch is its OWN test, because the patch is this project's and upstream's suite does not know about it.
exclude_reasons.util: Upstream's test-support helpers, which only its own tests use.
